newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS-BHP aims to slash copper costs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS-BHP aims to slash copper costs.

text.p: The world's second-largest copper producer, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP), said on Friday it aimed to slash production costs in North America to below 60 U.S. cents a pound and across-the-board to well below 50 cents.
BHP earlier on Friday said it has cut production costs in North America by about seven cents a pound in the quarter ended November 30 to just over 70 U.S. cents.
In the first quarter, the U.S. operations were running at 85 U.S. cents per pound due to lower ore grades and technical problems related to power supply.
"We are targetting another six cents there (North America) specific to the North American operations -- and a further five cents across the board," Prescott said.
He declined to give a target date for the cost reductions but said this would effectively lower North Armerican costs by another 11 U.S. cents per pound.
He said production costs at BHP's North American operations, acquired with the US$2.4 billion purchase of Magma Copper last January, were "just above 70 (cents) now".
BHP also plans to run its copper operations at "the highest level we can achieve" to counter the subdued outlook for world copper prices over the next two or three years, Prescott said.
Copper currently fetches about US$1.00 per pound on world markets.
Prescott said the market fundamentals for copper were sound, noting BHP was able to sell all it could produce.
In the current business year ending May 31, 1997, BHP expects to produce about one million tonnes of copper. Only Chile's state-run Codelco produces more copper.
"It's a cyclical industry and we think we are in the lower part of the cycle," Prescott said.
BHP said earlier on Friday that Magma Copper had swung back into profit in the second quarter, with a turnaround of A$37 million after tax from the first quarter.
Overall, BHP posted a first half net profit of A$790 million, a drop of 9.8 percent on the year-ago result. The group has minerals, petroleum, and steel operations alongside copper.
